title: My Family, My Things
overview: Name the people in a family. Say my phone, his key, their photo. Use a, an and the. Point and say this and these. Say one key, two keys.
learningPath: The lesson: listen, then say it.
Words: 26 words. Look, listen and say.
Patterns: 4 cards. Start with the one done for you.
Reading: 3 texts. Read them, then say them.
Speaking: tap the mic, say it, then listen back.
Writing: a family and your things. A made-up family is OK.
Practice: write it, then check the answers.
Quiz: 12 questions. Then look at My progress.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 2.
In this unit, you talk about a family and your things.
You can use a made-up family.
Listen.
This is my family.
This is my mother, and this is my father.
This is my brother. This is my sister.
Now, who has got the thing?
I: my. This is my phone.
You: your. Is this your key?
He: his. Ivan has got a book. It is his book.
She: her. Lena has got a watch. It is her watch.
We: our. This is our photo.
They: their. Mark and Zoe have got a baby. It is their baby.
His or her? Look at the person, not the thing.
Now a and the.
I have got a bag. The bag is on the bed.
Say a for one thing, the first time.
Say the when you know which one.
Uncle, aunt and umbrella start with a vowel sound.
Say an: an uncle, an aunt, an umbrella.
Many languages have no word like a or the. English needs them.
Now this and these.
One key: this is my key.
Two keys: these are my keys.
This goes with is. These goes with are.
Now one, and two or more.
One book, two books. Add s.
One phone, two phones.
One watch, two watches. Say one more beat: watch-es.
One baby, two babies.
Many languages have no ending here. English needs it.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

outcomes.evidence: Pattern 1 practice self-checked; Practice 1, eight items; Speaking 1 and 2 recordings; Writing 2 checklist; Quiz items 1 to 3.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say: This is her phone.

outcomes.outcome: Name the people in a family and read who is who in a short text.
outcomes.evidence: Reading 1 and 2, questions 1 to 7; Practice 2 matching; Quiz item 11.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can read who is who in a family.

outcomes.outcome: Write family words and things you carry with a, an or the in front: a key, an umbrella, the key.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 2 practice; Practice 3, eight items; Writing 1 checklist; Quiz items 4 to 6.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write a, an or the.

outcomes.outcome: Point to things and people with this and these, and ask and answer: What is this? What are these? Is this your key?
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 3 practice; Practice 4, eight items; Speaking 3 and 5 recordings; Quiz items 7 and 8.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can ask: What is this? What are these?

outcomes.outcome: Write and say one thing and two or more: key, keys; watch, watches; baby, babies.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 4 practice; Practice 5, ten items; Speaking 4 recording; Writing 3 checklist; Quiz items 9 and 10.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write one key, two keys.

outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can find my thing on a list.

words.meaning: Mother, father, sisters, brothers: the people in a home.
practice: Our family is in the photo.
Two families are on the bus.
My family and I live on Park Street.
words.starter: This is my family. This is my …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a family of four. It can be made up, or a family you know. Say This is my … for each person. Then ask the tutor to count the people.

words.meaning: A woman. She has got a son or a daughter.
practice: Her mother is from a small town.
Who is she? She is my mother.
Our mother has got a phone.
words.tutor: Say two lines about a made-up mother: This is my mother. Her name is … Ask the tutor to ask you Who is she? and answer with a whole line.

words.meaning: A man. He has got a son or a daughter.
words.example: His father is from a small town.
practice: Who is he? He is my father.
Their father has got a watch.
words.tutor: Say three lines about a made-up father with he and his, like He is my father. His name is Tomas. Ask the tutor to check you said his, not her.

words.meaning: A boy or a man. His mother and father are your mother and father.
words.starter: I have got a brother. His name is …
words.tutor: Ask the tutor Have you got a brother? Then tell it about a made-up brother: his name and his age, from 1 to 20.

words.meaning: A girl or a woman. Her mother and father are your mother and father.
practice: His sister has got a phone.
words.tutor: Say one sister or two sisters, five times, in any order. Ask the tutor to write which one it heard each time, then check.

words.meaning: The boy of a mother and a father. He can be a man now.
words.tutor: Son sounds like sun. The spelling is s-o-n. Ask the tutor to say son or sun in a line five times. Write which one each line needs.

words.meaning: The girl of a mother and a father. She can be a woman now.
words.tutor: Daughter is hard to spell: d-a-u-g-h-t-e-r. You do not hear the g and the h. Spell it to the tutor and ask it to check each letter.

words.meaning: A very small person. He or she is 0 or 1.
words.example: The baby is on the bed.
practice: This is my sister and her baby.
Is the baby a boy or a girl?
Two babies are in the photo.
words.tutor: Baby changes for two or more: babies. Ask the tutor for five words. Say each one for one and for two, like one baby, two babies.

words.meaning: The mother of your mother, or of your father.
practice: My grandmother is from a small town.
Her grandmother has got a watch.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor who is who: My grandmother is the mother of my father. Use a made-up family. Ask the tutor if each line is right.

words.meaning: The father of your mother, or of your father.
words.example: Our grandfather is in the photo.
practice: His grandfather has got a book.
Who is he? He is my grandfather.
The grandfather is on the bus.
words.tutor: Grandfather is grand and father. Say the two parts, then the whole word, to the tutor. Do the same for grandmother.

words.meaning: The brother of your mother, or of your father.
practice: My uncle is from a small town.
Her uncle has got a phone.
words.starter: I have got an uncle. He …
words.tutor: Uncle starts with a vowel sound, so you say an uncle. Ask the tutor for six family words and say a or an before each one.

words.meaning: The sister of your mother, or of your father.
practice: Our aunt has got two sons.
His aunt is on the phone.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up aunt: her name and her age. Check you said her each time, and an aunt, not a aunt.

words.meaning: The son or daughter of your uncle or aunt.
practice: Her cousins are from a small town.
words.tutor: A cousin can be a boy or a girl. Say two lines about made-up cousins, one with his and one with her. Ask the tutor to check both.

words.meaning: A person you like. He or she is not family.
practice: She is my friend from work.
He is my friend from school.
My friends are on the bus.
words.starter: This is my friend. Her name is …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a friend, at school or at work. You can make one up. Say his name or her name. His or her: look at the person.

words.meaning: He is 5, 10 or 15. He is not a man.
practice: Two boys are at the bus stop.
Is it a boy or a girl?
The boy has got a book.
words.tutor: Say a boy, the boy, two boys to the tutor. Then make one line with each, and ask it to check the a, the and s.

words.meaning: She is 5, 10 or 15. She is not a woman.
words.example: The girl has got a pencil.
practice: Two girls are in the photo.
A girl and a boy are here.
words.tutor: Girl has an l at the end. Say girl, girls, a girl, two girls to the tutor. Ask it: is the l clear in all four?

words.meaning: You talk to people on it. You can look at photos on it.
words.example: My phone is in my bag.
practice: Her phone is on the bed.
I have got a phone and a key.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor where your phone is now, like My phone is in my bag. Then say where two more things are, with in or on.

words.meaning: It opens a door.
practice: The key is in the box.
His keys are on the bus.
words.tutor: Key ends in y. For two, just add s: keys. Say one key, two keys, three keys to the tutor and ask it to check the s.

words.meaning: You read it. It has got words and pictures.
practice: The book is in my bag.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to say book, books, a book or the book at random six times. Write what you hear, then check.

words.meaning: It has got water in it. You can put it in a bag.
words.example: My bottle is in my bag.
words.tutor: Bottle has a double t in the middle. Spell bottle to the tutor, then bottles, and ask it to check both.

words.meaning: It is on your arm. It tells you the time.
words.example: Her watch is on the bed.
practice: The watch is in the box.
words.tutor: Watch changes for two: watches, with one more beat. Say one watch, two watches, three watches to the tutor, and ask if it heard the extra beat.

words.meaning: It writes, like a pen. You can fix a mistake.
practice: I have got a pen and a pencil.
The pencil is in the bag.
words.starter: I have got a pencil and …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor four things in a bag: a pencil, a pen, a book, an umbrella. Ask it to check every a and an.

words.meaning: It has got your name on it: a bus card, a library card.
practice: The card is in my bag.
Her card has got her name on it.
words.tutor: Name two cards you can have, like a bus card and a library card. Say This is my … card for each, and ask the tutor to repeat them back.

words.meaning: It stops the rain. You are not wet.
practice: Two umbrellas are on the bus.
Her umbrella is in the bag.
words.tutor: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so an umbrella. Say an umbrella, the umbrella, two umbrellas to the tutor in that order.

words.meaning: A picture from a phone.
words.example: This is a photo of my family.
practice: The photo is on my phone.
words.starter: This is a photo of my …
words.tutor: Describe a made-up family photo to the tutor in three lines, starting This is. Ask it to ask you Who is this? and answer it.

words.meaning: A drawing or a photo. You look at it.
practice: This is a picture of my aunt.
The pictures are in the book.
words.tutor: Picture ends like pic-cher. Say picture and pictures to the tutor, and ask it to check the end of each word.

grammar.title: my, your, his, her, our, their
grammar.explanation:
Say who has got the thing.
Put my, your, his, her, our or their first.
Then say the thing: my phone.
His or her? Look at the person.
grammar.rule:
I — my
This is my phone.

you — your
Is this your key?

he — his
Ivan has got a book. It is his book.

she — her
Lena has got a watch. It is her watch.

we — our
This is our photo.

they — their
Mark and Zoe have got a baby. It is their baby.

his: a man or a boy has got it.
her: a woman or a girl has got it.
grammar.workedExample:
Zoe and ___ brother.
1. Look at the person: Zoe.
2. Zoe is a girl: she.
3. She goes with her.
4. Look at Zoe, not the brother.
5. Write: Zoe and her brother.
grammar.mistake:
Look at the person, not the thing.
No: Ivan and her sister.
Yes: Ivan and his sister.
Ivan is a man, so his.
grammar.tip: He: his. She: her. They: their.
grammar.practice:
Write my, your, his, her, our or their.
1. I have got a phone. It is ___ phone.
2. Ivan has got a key. It is ___ key.
3. Lena has got a book. It is ___ book.
4. Mark and Zoe have got a map. It is ___ map.
5. We have got a photo. It is ___ photo.
6. Hello, Sam! Is this ___ pen?
7. Mark and ___ sister.
8. Lena and ___ uncle.
grammar.answers:
1. my  2. his  3. her  4. their  5. our  6. your  7. his  8. her
Wrong on 7 or 8? Look at the person, not the family word. Mark is a man: his. Lena is a woman: her.

grammar.title: a key, an aunt, the key
grammar.explanation:
Say a for one thing, the first time.
Say the when you know which one.
Say an before a vowel sound.
Many languages have no word like a or the. English needs them.
grammar.rule:
a — one thing, the first time
I have got a key.
This is a photo.

the — you know which one
The key is in my bag.
The photo is on my phone.

an — before a vowel sound
an uncle
an aunt
an umbrella

my, not a my
This is my key.
grammar.workedExample:
I have got ___ umbrella. ___ umbrella is wet.
1. First time: a or an.
2. Umbrella starts with a vowel sound: an.
3. Next time, you know which one: the.
4. Write: I have got an umbrella. The umbrella is wet.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to leave out a or the.
No: I have got phone.
Yes: I have got a phone.
No: Phone is in my bag.
Yes: The phone is in my bag.
grammar.tip: First time: a. Next time: the.
grammar.practice:
Write a, an or the.
1. I have got ___ book.
2. I have got a book. ___ book is in my bag.
3. This is ___ pencil.
4. She has got ___ aunt.
5. I have got ___ umbrella.
6. I have got a card. ___ card is on the bus.
7. Is this ___ key?
grammar.answers:
1. a  2. The  3. a  4. an  5. an  6. The  7. a
Wrong on 4 or 5? Aunt and umbrella start with a vowel sound: an.
Wrong on 2 or 6? You know which one now: the.

grammar.title: This is, these are
grammar.explanation:
Point at one thing or person: this.
Point at two or more: these.
This goes with is.
These goes with are.
grammar.rule:
one — this is
This is my key.
This is my sister.
What is this? It is a watch.
Who is this? This is my uncle.

two or more — these are
These are my keys.
These are my sisters.
What are these? They are pencils.
grammar.workedExample:
___ my photos.
1. Look at the end: photos. An s, so two or more.
2. Two or more: these.
3. These goes with are.
4. Write: These are my photos.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to say is after these.
No: These is my keys.
Yes: These are my keys.
No: This are my book.
Yes: This is my book.
grammar.tip: This: one. These: two or more.
grammar.practice:
Write This is or These are.
1. ___ my phone.
2. ___ my books.
3. ___ our photos.
4. ___ her watch.
5. ___ my brother.
6. ___ their keys.
7. ___ my cousins, Mark and Zoe.
grammar.answers:
1. This is  2. These are  3. These are  4. This is  5. This is  6. These are  7. These are
Wrong on 7? Mark and Zoe are two people, so these.
Look at the end of the word: an s means two or more.

grammar.title: One key, two keys
grammar.explanation:
Two or more? Add s to the word.
One key, two keys.
A few words change a little.
Look at the list.
grammar.rule:
Add s:
a key — two keys
a book — three books
a phone — four phones
an uncle — two uncles

After ch or x, add es:
a watch — two watches
a box — two boxes

A y after b or l changes to ies:
a baby — two babies
a family — two families

Key is not like baby: e comes before the y, so keys.

No a before two or more: my keys, not a keys.
grammar.workedExample:
I have got three ___. (watch)
1. Three: two or more. Add an ending.
2. Watch ends in ch.
3. After ch, add es.
4. Write: I have got three watches.
5. Say it: watch-es, one more beat.
grammar.mistake:
Easy to miss: the s after a number.
No: two book.
Yes: two books.
No: I have got three sister.
Yes: I have got three sisters.
grammar.tip: One: no s. Two or more: add s.
grammar.practice:
Write the word for two or more.
1. one pen, two ___
2. one key, three ___
3. one watch, two ___
4. one baby, two ___
5. one cousin, four ___
6. one bottle, six ___
7. one box, two ___
8. one photo, ten ___
grammar.answers:
1. pens  2. keys  3. watches  4. babies  5. cousins  6. bottles  7. boxes  8. photos
Wrong on 3 or 7? After ch or x, add es.
Wrong on 4? Baby: the y changes, babies.
Wrote keies on 2? Key has e before the y, so just add s: keys.

readings.title: A Family Photo
readings.passage:
Look at this photo.
This is my family.
This is my mother. Her name is Lena.
This is my father. His name is Ivan.
These are my brothers, Sam and Mark.
The baby is my sister. Her name is Zoe.
I am the girl. I have got a book.

readings.title: Who Is Who in a Family
readings.setting: Words for the people in a family.
readings.passage:
Your mother and father have got a son and a daughter.
The son is your brother. The daughter is your sister.
The mother of your mother is your grandmother.
The father of your mother is your grandfather.
The brother of your mother is your uncle.
The sister of your mother is your aunt.
Her son is your cousin.

readings.title: Lost Property at the Bus Station
readings.setting: A desk at a bus station.
readings.passage:
BUS STATION
LOST PROPERTY
Things from the buses:

Bus 5: 2 phones, 1 watch
Bus 12: 3 umbrellas, 1 bottle
Bus 16: 4 keys, 1 book

Is it your thing?
Go to Desk 3.
Say your name and your bus number.
Bus card, please.

comprehension.q: What is the name of the mother?
comprehension.why: Line 3: This is my mother. Her name is Lena.

comprehension.q: Is Ivan a man or a woman?
comprehension.a: A man. He is the father.
comprehension.why: Line 4: This is my father. His name is Ivan. His is for a man.

comprehension.q: Sam and Mark: are they brothers or cousins?
comprehension.why: Line 5: These are my brothers, Sam and Mark.

comprehension.a: The baby. She is a sister.
comprehension.why: Line 6: The baby is my sister. Her name is Zoe.

comprehension.q: Who is the sister of your mother?
comprehension.why: Line 6: The sister of your mother is your aunt.

comprehension.q: The daughter of your mother and father: who is she?
comprehension.why: Line 2: The daughter is your sister.

comprehension.q: Line 7: Her son is your cousin. Her: who is she?
comprehension.why: Line 6 is about your aunt. So her in line 7 is your aunt.
The list says: Bus 12: 3 umbrellas, 1 bottle.

comprehension.q: Your phone is on bus 5. Where do you go?
comprehension.why: The notice says: Is it your thing? Go to Desk 3.

comprehension.q: You are at Desk 3. What do you say?
comprehension.a: My name and my bus number.
comprehension.why: The notice says: Say your name and your bus number. Bus card, please.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — My phone, his book
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
This is my phone.
Is this your key?
It is his book.
It is her watch.
This is our photo.
It is their bottle.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: my, your, his, her, our, their. All 6?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name a person and a thing, like Lena and a card. Say the line, like It is her card. Do this six times.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — This is my family
speaking.instructions:
Use a made-up family, or a family you know.
Say 5 lines.
This is my ___.
His name is ___.
This is my ___.
Her name is ___.
These are my ___.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: his for a man or a boy?
Her for a woman or a girl?
Are after these?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Use a made-up family, or a family you know.
Say 5 lines.
This is my …
His name is …
This is my …
Her name is …
These are my …
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: his for a man or a boy?
Her for a woman or a girl?
Are after these?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor about your made-up family in five lines. Ask it to ask you Who is this? about two people, and answer each one.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — What is this? What are these?
speaking.instructions:
Listen to each question. Look at the word. Say the answer.
1. What is this? A phone.
2. What are these? Keys.
3. What is this? An umbrella.
4. What are these? Books.
5. What is this? A watch.
Say it like this: It is a phone. They are keys.
Tap the mic. Say the 5 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check: it is for one thing?
They are for two or more?
An before umbrella?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to ask What is this? or What are these? about eight things. Answer each with It is a … or They are …

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — One book, two books
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
one key, two keys
one phone, two phones
one book, two books
one card, two cards
one watch, two watches
one baby, two babies
Watches has one more beat: watch-es.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: an s on each second word?
One more beat in watches?
speaking.tutor: Say ten things to the tutor, one and then two, like one bottle, two bottles. Ask it to tell you any word with no s at the end.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Is this your key?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Is this your phone? B: Yes, it is my phone. Thanks!
2. A: Is this your key? B: No, it is her key.
3. A: Who is this? B: This is my cousin.
4. A: Are these your books? B: Yes, these are my books.
5. A: Is this his umbrella? B: No, it is their umbrella.
Tap the mic. Say the 5 B lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: my, her or their in each B line?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be A and ask about five things. Answer each one with Yes, it is my … or No, it is his … or her …

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — At the lost property desk
speaking.instructions:
You are at Desk 3 at a bus station.
Your umbrella is on bus 12.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello!
You: Hello. My umbrella is on bus 12.
Desk: What is your name, please?
You: My name is ___.
Desk: Is this your umbrella?
You: No, it is not my umbrella.
Desk: Is this your umbrella?
You: Yes! This is my umbrella. Thanks!
Desk: Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up name.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? My in lines 1 to 4?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
You are at Desk 3 at a bus station.
Your umbrella is on bus 12.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello!
You: Hello. My umbrella is on bus 12.
Desk: What is your name, please?
You: My name is …
Desk: Is this your umbrella?
You: No, it is not my umbrella.
Desk: Is this your umbrella?
You: Yes! This is my umbrella. Thanks!
Desk: Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up name.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? My in lines 1 to 4?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be the person at the lost property desk. Tell it your thing and your bus number, then answer its questions.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Family words
writing.prompt:
Write 8 family words.
Write a or an before each one.
writing.model:
a mother
a father
a brother
a sister
a baby
an uncle
an aunt
a cousin
writing.criteria:
8 words.
A or an before each one.
An before uncle and aunt.
Each spelling checked on the Words page.
writing.support:
Copy 4 words from the Words page.
Say each one, then write it.
Then write 4 more.
writing.extension: Write 4 of them for two or more: two sisters, two uncles.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A family photo
writing.prompt:
Write about a family photo.
Use a made-up family, or a family you know.
Write 6 lines. Use his and her.
writing.model:
This is my family.
This is my aunt.
Her name is Eva.
This is my uncle.
His name is Dan.
These are my cousins.
writing.criteria:
6 lines.
His for a man or a boy.
Her for a woman or a girl.
These are for two or more.
A capital letter at the start.
A full stop (.) at the end.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the names.
Change aunt and uncle to two other family words.
writing.extension: Add 2 lines about a baby: The baby is my … Her name is … or His name is …

writing.title: Writing 3 — In my bag
writing.prompt:
What is in your bag?
Write 5 lines.
Use a, an or the.
Write one thing for two or more.
writing.model:
I have got a bag.
The bag is on the bus.
I have got a phone and a key.
I have got an umbrella.
I have got two pencils.
writing.criteria:
5 lines.
A, an or the before each one thing.
An before umbrella.
One word with s for two or more.
A full stop (.) at the end of each line.
writing.support:
First write the things: bag, phone, key.
Then write I have got a in front.
Check: an before umbrella?
writing.extension: Add a line with these: These are my keys.

writing.title: Writing 4 — A lost property card
writing.prompt:
Your thing is on a bus.
Write a card for the lost property desk.
You can use a made-up name.
writing.model:
LOST PROPERTY
Name: TOMAS
Bus: 16
Things: two keys and a book
writing.criteria:
3 lines: name, bus, things.
The name in capital letters.
The bus as a number.
A or an before one thing.
An s for two or more.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the name.
Use a bus and things from Reading 3.
writing.extension: Write a card for a friend or someone in your family. Use his or her: His things: a watch.

activities.title: Practice 1 — My, his, her, their
activities.instructions:
Write my, your, his, her, our or their.
1. Mark has got a phone. It is ___ phone.
2. Zoe has got a card. It is ___ card.
3. I have got a key. It is ___ key.
4. Lena and Ivan have got a baby. It is ___ baby.
5. We have got a photo. It is ___ photo.
6. Hello, Sam. Is this ___ bottle?
7. Ivan and ___ grandmother.
8. Zoe and ___ brother.
activities.answers:
1. his  2. her  3. my  4. their  5. our  6. your  7. his  8. her
Check 7 and 8: look at the person first. Ivan: his. Zoe: her.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write your answers on paper. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Who is who?
activities.instructions:
Match 1 to 6 with a to f.
1. the mother of your father
2. the brother of your mother
3. the son of your aunt
4. the sister of your father
5. the father of your mother
6. the daughter of your mother and father
a. your aunt
b. your grandfather
c. your sister
d. your grandmother
e. your cousin
f. your uncle
activities.answers:
1d  2f  3e  4a  5b  6c
Check 3: the son of your aunt is your cousin, not your brother.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read Reading 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Read each line out loud. Write the letter. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — a, an or the
activities.instructions:
Write a, an or the.
1. I have got ___ pencil.
2. She has got ___ umbrella.
3. I have got a bottle. ___ bottle is in my bag.
4. Is this ___ card?
5. He has got ___ uncle.
6. I have got a watch. ___ watch is on the bed.
7. This is ___ photo of my family.
8. We have got a map. ___ map is in the box.
activities.answers:
1. a  2. an  3. The  4. a  5. an  6. The  7. a  8. The
Wrong on 2 or 5? Umbrella and uncle start with a vowel sound: an.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud. Write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — This is or these are
activities.instructions:
Write This is or These are.
1. ___ my keys.
2. ___ my umbrella.
3. ___ our friends.
4. ___ his photo.
5. ___ her cousins.
6. ___ my pencil.
7. ___ their books.
8. ___ my grandfather.
activities.answers:
1. These are  2. This is  3. These are  4. This is  5. These are  6. This is  7. These are  8. This is
Look at the end of the word: an s means two or more.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud. Write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — One, two or more
activities.instructions:
Write the word for two or more.
1. one phone, two ___
2. one girl, three ___
3. one watch, two ___
4. one family, two ___
5. one umbrella, four ___
6. one card, five ___
7. one key, two ___
8. one baby, three ___
9. one friend, six ___
10. one picture, two ___
activities.answers:
1. phones  2. girls  3. watches  4. families  5. umbrellas  6. cards  7. keys  8. babies  9. friends  10. pictures
Watch: after ch, add es.
Family and baby: the y changes, ies.
Key: e before the y, so just s.
9 or 10 right: good.
8 or less: read Pattern 4 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say one and two out loud. Write the word. Check each letter with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Find it on the list
activities.instructions:
Look at Reading 3. Write the bus number.
1. 2 phones: bus ___
2. 4 keys: bus ___
3. 1 bottle: bus ___
4. 1 book: bus ___
5. 3 umbrellas: bus ___
6. 1 watch: bus ___
activities.answers:
1. 5  2. 16  3. 12  4. 16  5. 12  6. 5
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read the list again, one line at a time.
activities.solo: Put your finger on each line of the list. Find the thing. Write the bus. Check with the key.

quizzes.q: Ivan has got a book. It is ___ book.
quizzes.why: Ivan is a man, so his. Her is for a woman. He goes before is: He is Ivan. Their is for two or more people.
Look at Lena, not the brother. Lena is a woman, so her. His is for a man. She goes before is. Is is not for a person.

quizzes.q: Mark and Zoe have got a phone. It is ___ phone.
quizzes.why: Mark and Zoe are two people, so their. His is for one man. Her is for one woman. They goes before are: They are 18.
Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so an. A is for words like a key. These is for two or more. Never write a after my.

quizzes.q: I have got a key. ___ key is in my bag.
quizzes.why: You know which key now, so the key. An is for a vowel sound, like an aunt. These is for two or more. Is is not a word for a thing.
Aunt starts with a vowel sound: an aunt. Key does not start with a vowel sound: a key. No a before my: my aunt.
Keys ends in s: two or more, so these. These goes with are. This and it are for one thing. He is for one man.
One photo: this is. This goes with is, not are. For two or more, say: These are my photos.
After ch, add es: watches. Watchs has no e. Watch is for one. Ies is for words like baby.
Baby: the y changes, so babies. Babys and babyes keep the y. Baby is for one. Key is not like this: keys.

quizzes.q: The mother of your father is your ___.
quizzes.why: The mother of your mother or father: your grandmother. A grandfather is a man. Grandmothers is two or more. An aunt is the sister of your mother or father.

quizzes.q: Reading 3: your key is on a bus. Where do you go?
quizzes.why: The notice says: Is it your thing? Go to Desk 3. The keys are on bus 16, not bus 12. Park Street and a bin are not on it.

teacherNotes.note: A learner can finish every part of this unit with nobody beside them: each card shows one item done step by step before its practice, each exercise ends with a key and a score line, and each speaking task ends with record, listen back and a short visible check. If you are helping, listen to a recording together and point to the checklist, rather than stopping the learner mid-line.

teacherNotes.type: Family is never a real-life question
teacherNotes.note: Every family task accepts a made-up family or a family the learner knows, and says so. Some learners live far from their family, some have lost people, some have no son or daughter and never will. Do not ask who is really in their family, and never correct a made-up one. The same goes for the lost property card: a made-up name is fine.

teacherNotes.type: The one error worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: His and her follow the person who has the thing, not the thing: Ivan and his sister, never Ivan and her sister. In many languages one word covers both, or the word follows the thing, so this error is logical rather than careless. It is also invisible in writing unless you check who the owner is, which is why Practice 1 items 7 and 8 test exactly that.

An is taught only as far as this unit forces it: uncle, aunt and umbrella. Things you cannot count (some rice), possessive 's (Sara's bag), that and those, mine and yours, and irregular plurals such as child and children all come in Unit 8, so this unit writes the mother of your father rather than your father's mother. Men and women are not used as plurals here for the same reason.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marker, and no task here is scored by it alone. Every tutor prompt that involves a person uses a made-up family, friend or name. Keep that wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor real names, ages or family details.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say: This is her phone.
I can read who is who in a family.
I can write a, an or the.
I can ask: What is this? What are these?
I can write one key, two keys.
I can find my thing on a list.

assignment.title: My family, my things
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Talk about a family photo in 5 lines. Use this, these, his and her. You can use a made-up family.
2. Write 5 lines about the things in your bag, like Writing 3. Use a, an or the, and one word for two or more.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and five written lines
